source.citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

authority_note: Facts are condensed/paraphrased from the cited printed treatments and relevant keys; unmentioned morphology is not assumed absent. Source pagination is printed book pagination.

bonap.scope: Hays County plus west/north target counties
bonap.note: Flora distribution is not a substitute for BONAP county nativity.

records.leaves: Blades to 5 cm × 2 cm; petioles to 1 cm
records.flowers: Single or paired in terminal one-sided spike-like inflorescences; calyx ca. 5 mm; reddish two-lipped corolla 30–40 mm, upper lip nearly entire, lower 3-lobed; 2 stamens
records.habitat: Native Edwards Plateau; planted and sometimes escapes

records.flowers: Axillary short-peduncled to subsessile clusters, involucre of 2–4 floral bracts; obovate bracts to 7 × 2–5 mm; pink to purple (rare white) corollas 15–20 mm, upper lip entire or shallow 2-lobed, lower usually entire
records.fruit: Stipitate ovoid emarginate capsule 5–6 mm; 2–4 seeds
records.habitat: Moist wooded stream bottoms and wet habitats

records.habit: Rhizomatous ± pubescent perennial; erect or partly decumbent stems 7–30 cm
records.leaves: Sessile linear to oblanceolate obtuse blades
records.flowers: Sessile axillary flowers shorter than leaves, foliaceous bracts; sepals united ca. 1/4, acuminate lobes 9–13 mm; lavender corolla with dark throat dots 15–27 mm

records.habit: Glabrous rhizomatous colonial perennial; erect stems to ca. 100 cm
records.leaves: Sessile or nearly so; narrowly oblong-lanceolate to elliptic-lanceolate
records.flowers: Axillary peduncled dense spikes to 3 cm; peduncles to 15 cm; sepals linear-lanceolate ca. 7 mm, nearly free; white or violet corollas 10–12 mm with red-purple spots; genus treatment describes two stamens and 3-lobed lower lip
records.fruit: Capsule ca. 12 mm; genus treatment four-seeded
records.habitat: Wet ground, stream and pond margins
records.nomenclature: POWO accepts Dianthera americana; ITIS accepts Justicia americana; keep both taxonomic perspectives

records.habit: Perennial to ca. 0.75 m; densely pubescent with short spreading to appressed hairs
records.flowers: Flora key: sessile or short-peduncled axillary glomerules at multiple nodes, broader leaves; fruits minutely canescent ca. 10 mm
records.habitat: Wooded riparian often rocky areas; Texas endemic per flora

records.habit: Perennial to ca. 0.8 m; usually rather densely short-pilose
records.leaves: Lanceolate to ovate or broadly elliptic; sessile or subsessile with petioles to 3 mm, erect-ascending
records.flowers: Flora key: axillary nearly sessile or short-peduncled clustered flowers; linear calyx lobes with slender tips

records.leaves: Petiolate, oblong-lanceolate to narrowly ovate-oblong, 3–12 cm long, undulate to toothed
records.flowers: Terminal long-peduncled panicle-like inflorescence; usually white sometimes pale bluish purple, corolla (5–)5.5–6.5 cm; calyx lobes 14–20 mm in flower; some early axillary cleistogamous flowers
records.habitat: Limestone outcrops, gravel, thickets and open woods

records.habit: Stems spreading-pilose becoming glabrate, to 0.7 m
records.flowers: Flowers opening near sunrise and falling in afternoon; key distinguishes long-peduncled terminal panicle-like inflorescence; violet-lavender curved corolla ca. 4–5(–5.5) cm; calyx lobes 10–15 mm; sepals with gland-tipped hairs or hispid to slightly scabrous
records.nomenclature: POWO treats Ruellia nudiflora as synonym of Ruellia ciliatiflora; 1999 flora uses infraspecific name. Confirm circumscription before transferring all variety-level claims.
